text: Tel-Hai College - Course 199934 Introduction to Quantum Computing Lecture-07 Prof. Ofer Shir ofersh@telhai.ac.il Spring 2025 Shir Tel-Hai: intro2QC (199934) Spring 2025 1 / 19 -- 1 of 19 -- Quantum Optimization Approaches There are two primary approaches to quantum optimization: 1 Quantum Annealing: This approach, exemplified by D-Wave Systems, leverages a physical process to find the ground state of a quantum system. It is well-suited for combinatorial optimization problems. 2 Gate-based Quantum Computing: This approach, employed by companies like IBM and Google, uses quantum gates to manipulate qubits and solve optimization problems. It offers greater flexibility but requires more complex algorithms. J > 0 (Ferromagnetic – spins tend to align) or J < 0 ( Antiferromagnetic – spins anti-align) • External Magnetic Field (h): Spins also interact with an external magnetic field. • Hamiltonian: The energy of the system is given by: H = − ∑ 〈i,j〉 Jij sisj − μ ∑ i hisi • Significance: Fundamental model for understanding critical phenomena and statistical me

the system is given by: H = − ∑ 〈i,j〉 Jij sisj − μ ∑ i hisi • Significance: Fundamental model for understanding critical phenomena and statistical mechanics – but also in neural networks, social modeling. Quantum Annealing: • A method to solve optimization problems by evolving a quantum system from a simple initia

, the system stays in the ground state. Quantum Annealing: • A method to solve optimization problems by evolving a quantum system from a simple initial Hamiltonian Hi to a final Hamiltonian Hf encoding the problem. • The time-dependent Hamiltonian is given by: H(t) = (1 − s(t))Hi + s(t)Hf where s(t) interpolates from 0 to 1 as t goes from 0 to T . Shir Tel-Hai: intro2QC (199934) Spring 2025 8 / 19 -- 8 of 19 -- Adiabatic Theorem and Quantum Annealing (2/2) Initial and Final Hamiltonians: • Initial Hamiltonian Hi: A simple Hamiltonian whose ground state is easy to prepare. Hi = − ∑ i sx i • Final Hamiltonian Hf : Encodes the optimization problem, Hf = − ∑ 〈i,j〉 Jij sz i sz j − ∑ i hisz i where Jij and hi represent the problem constraints and local fields. Adiabatic Condition: • To ensure the system remains in the ground state, the evolution must be slow enough: dH(t) dt  ∆2 where ∆ is th

local fields. Adiabatic Condition: • To ensure the system remains in the ground state, the evolution must be slow enough: dH(t) dt  ∆2 where ∆ is the energy gap between the ground state and first excited state. Shir Tel-Hai: intro2QC (199934) Spring 2025 9 / 19 -- 9 of 19 -- Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization The Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization (QUBO) problem can be formulated as finding a binary vector x ∈ {0, 1}n that solves: minimize xT Qx Q is an n × n matrix of real coefficients representing the quadratic terms: A matrix where each element Qij represents the interaction between the binary variables xi and xj . The idea: draw analogy Ising model ⇐⇒ QUBO optimization: [Ising]: ∑ i,j Jij sisj − ∑ i hisi ⇐⇒ [QUBO]: xT Qx Shir Tel-Hai: intro2QC (199934) Spring 2025 10 / 19 -- 10 of 19 -- topology Unlike theoretical modeling, in quantum annealing hardware there are

T Qx Shir Tel-Hai: intro2QC (199934) Spring 2025 10 / 19 -- 10 of 19 -- topology Unlike theoretical modeling, in quantum annealing hardware there are no connections among all qubit pairs (D-Wave 2000Q QPU): inner-cell topology intra-cell topology Shir Tel-Hai: intro2QC (199934) Spring 2025 11 / 19 -- 11 of 19 -- embedding To solve a problem expressed as an Ising model on a quantum computer, the variables of the Ising model needs to be assigned to physical qubits. The interaction strength between two qubits can be controlled only if there is a physical connection between two qubits. This means that variables in the Ising model that appear together in a quadratic term must be assigned to qubits with a physical connection. This is done by a procedure by the name of “Minor Embedding”. Shir Tel-Hai: intro2QC (199934) Spring 2025 12 / 19 -- 12 of 19 -- D-Wave’s Pegasus architecture Shir Tel-Ha

ocedure by the name of “Minor Embedding”. Shir Tel-Hai: intro2QC (199934) Spring 2025 12 / 19 -- 12 of 19 -- D-Wave’s Pegasus architecture Shir Tel-Hai: intro2QC (199934) Spring 2025 13 / 19 -- 13 of 19 -- basic QUBO problem formulation The QUBO model is expressed by the optimization problem: minimize/maximize f := xT Qx x is an n-dimensional binary vector (x ∈ {0, 1}n): A vector where each element is either 0 or 1. The elements represent binary decision variables in the optimization problem. The Q matrix is assumed to be symmetric or in upper triangular form: Symmetric form: For all i and j except i = j, replace qij by (qij + qji)/2. Upper triangular form: For all i and j with j > i, replace qij by qij + qji. Then replace all qij for j < i by 0. Formally, the MAX-CUT problem involves finding a partition of the vertices of a graph G = (V, E) into two disjoint subsets such that the number of edges between the two subsets is maximized. For each vertex vi ∈ V , let xi be a binary decision variable such that: • xi = 0 if vertex vi is in subset V0 • xi = 1 if vertex vi is in subset V1 The edge (i, j) is cut if xi 6 = xj , which is indicated by xi +

uch that: • xi = 0 if vertex vi is in subset V0 • xi = 1 if vertex vi is in subset V1 The edge (i, j) is cut if xi 6 = xj , which is indicated by xi + xj − 2xixj . It is well-suited for combinatorial optimization problems. 2 Gate-based Quantum Computing: This approach, employed by companies like IBM and Google, uses quantum gates to manipulate qubits and solve optimization problems. It offers greater flexibility but requires more complex algorithms. The elements represent binary decision variables in the optimization problem. The Q matrix is assumed to be symmetric or in upper triangular form: Symmetric form: For all i and j except i = j, replace qij by (qij + qji)/2. Upper triangular form: For all i and j with j > i, replace qij by qij + qji. Then replace all qij for j < i by 0.
